name: Stan Getz and Luiz Bonfá
hook: An American tenor saxophonist and a Brazilian guitarist's one joint bossa nova session, dug up three decades later for a Pharcyde hit.

blurb.age7: Stan Getz played saxophone and Luiz Bonfá played guitar on a jazz record from Brazil. Years later, a rap group used a piece of it in one of their songs.
blurb.age13: American saxophonist Stan Getz and Brazilian guitarist Luiz Bonfá, key figures in bringing bossa nova to American jazz audiences, recorded the album 'Jazz Samba Encore!' together in New York in 1963. Its track 'Saudade Vem Correndo' was sampled by producer J Dilla for The Pharcyde's 'Runnin'' (1995), one of his first productions to reach an audience outside Detroit.
blurb.adult: Getz and Bonfá are on this map for a single joint record rather than their much larger individual careers, on the same 'sample hub' basis as Bob James and Ahmad Jamal (Q21): jazz is a deferred lineage here (BACKLOG), so figures from it appear only where a documented sample connects them to an artist already on the graph.

signatureTracks.title: Saudade Vem Correndo
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: From 'Jazz Samba Encore!' (Verve); its guitar and flute figure is the source for The Pharcyde's 'Runnin''.
